subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should OpenClaw treat slow or wedged Docker sandbox preparation as a bounded fail-soft condition by default, and should that ship through the existing open timeout PR or a replacement?
rationale: The source-level hang is real, but the exact OrbStack substep is not isolated and the likely fix changes default availability behavior for slow Docker control-plane operations.

options.title: Refresh and complete the timeout path
options.body: Adopt or replace the open timeout PR, cover prune/hash/backend waits, document any config/default surface, and require redacted real Docker or OrbStack proof before merge.

options.title: Instrument before changing defaults
options.body: Add targeted prep-stage diagnostics first so maintainers can confirm whether the cold-start stalls are Docker exec, prune, workspace layout, or Docker user resolution before selecting a fail-soft policy.

options.title: Scope this to the wedged-Docker issue only
options.body: Let the narrower wedged-Docker candidate land first, then re-review this broader cold-start issue with new evidence before closing it.

recommendation.title: Refresh and complete the timeout path
recommendation.body: Adopt or replace the open timeout PR, cover prune/hash/backend waits, document any config/default surface, and require redacted real Docker or OrbStack proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans sandbox architecture, prune/runtime cleanup, and default fail-soft behavior where the history shows repeated ownership-adjacent work.
